text:
Ariana Chen: quick sync — AcmeCorp was impacted by yesterday's incident (regional latency + 5xxs). Need: 1) a short customer-facing note, 2) status page copy, 3) SLA credit calc + evidence, 4) owners for follow-ups. I put a draft below. tagging @Jamal for timeline, @Marta for technical detail, @Legal for wording signoff.

incident-bot: Incident 2026-07-22-0312 triggered -> sev-2 latency spike in ap-northeast-1. Pager sent to oncall.

Jamal Ortiz: timeline I have from oncall notes:
```
02:12 UTC — Pager fired: p95 inference latency > 3s and 502 spikes observed
02:18 UTC — initial triage, identified model K/V cache thrash after rollout
02:30 UTC — rolled back model to previous variant
02:47 UTC — traffic routed to us-east failover for affected tenants
03:05 UTC — error rates returned to baseline, monitoring alerts cleared
03:20 UTC — incident declared mitigated, started post-incident data collection
```
We had ~35 minutes of elevated errors before failover. Some customers (AcmeCorp) reported timeouts for a few endpoints during the window.

Marta Kovac: adding tech context — root cause was a KV-cache eviction bug triggered by new model metadata size. During rollout, cache thrash caused tail latency to spike and some worker threads to return 502. Mitigation steps taken: rollback, cache parameter patch, increase cache budget, and add a health-check gate to rollout pipeline. Planned follow-ups:
- backport cache guard to 2 last releases (owner: @Marta)
- add rollout circuit-breaker that prevents parallel cache reinitialization (owner: eng-runtime)
- add canary traffic threshold at 0.5% for next 2 weeks (owner: eng-platform)

Evan Li: customer draft (please edit):
"Hi Acme team — we're sorry for the disruption on July 22. Between 02:12–03:05 UTC you may have experienced elevated latency and intermittent 502 errors on inference endpoints. We've identified the cause (cache eviction triggered during a model rollout), reverted the rollout, and implemented immediate mitigations. We're performing further fixes to prevent recurrence and will send a technical follow-up with more details in 72 hours.

As a gesture for the disruption, we'll apply an SLA credit to your account for the affected window. We'll confirm the amount and post the credit within 5 business days. If you need a call, we can schedule one. — Redwood Inference Support"

Priya Nair: SLA credit calc suggestion: per contract Section 4, downtime-based credit = min( (minutes of downtime / SLA window minutes) * monthly fee, cap ). For AcmeCorp they reported ~35 minutes of elevated errors. If we treat that as downtime:
```
Example: monthly fee = $12,000
SLA window (billing month minutes) = 43,200
Credit = (35 / 43200) * 12000 = ~$97.22
```
Recommend rounding to $100 credit and note the exact minutes in the communication. Also include a link to the support ticket and logs as evidence.

Legal: suggestion — keep wording factual and avoid speculative language about "root cause" until we finish RCA. Replace "We've identified the cause" with "Our investigation indicates" and commit to sending the full RCA. Also confirm we can promise a credit amount (Finance OK?). Remove language implying liability beyond contract.

Ariana Chen: updated draft with Legal tweaks:
"Hi Acme team — we're sorry for the disruption on July 22. Between 02:12–03:05 UTC you may have experienced elevated latency and intermittent 502 errors on inference endpoints. Our investigation indicates the issue was related to cache reinitialization during a model rollout; we reverted the rollout and applied mitigations. We're preparing a fuller RCA and will share it within 72 hours. Per your contract, we'll apply an SLA credit for the affected window; we'll confirm the exact amount and post it to your account within 5 business days. If you'd like a synchronous review, please let us know a few times that work for you. — Redwood Inference Support"

Marta Kovac: internal note — timeline statement is fine but please include the mitigation summary for the technical follow-up: rollback performed at 02:30 UTC, failover at 02:47 UTC, cache param patch at 03:10 UTC.

Evan Li: status page copy suggestion (short):
"Incident (July 22) — partial service disruption in ap-northeast-1 caused increased latency and transient 502s for some customers between 02:12–03:05 UTC. Root cause under investigation; mitigation applied. See customer communication for details."

Priya Nair: action items and owners I recommend including in the follow-up email so customers know next steps:
- final RCA (72 hours) — owner: @Marta
- preventive rollout gating changes (2 weeks) — owner: eng-platform
- credit applied (5 business days) — owner: finance/accounting
- offer for customer call (ASAP) — owner: cs-acct-team

incident-bot: Incident 2026-07-22-0312 closed by Jamal Ortiz at 03:25 UTC. Postmortem scheduled.

Legal: approved the customer-facing wording with the "investigation indicates" tweak. Requests that we record the exact logs we will attach to the credit justification.

Ariana Chen: final checklist before send:
- [x] Customer draft reviewed by Legal
- [x] SLA calc proposed ($100) — confirm with Finance
- [x] Status page short copy ready
- [ ] Attach logs and ticket links (Marta/Jamal)
- [ ] Confirm credit posting window with Finance (Priya)

Jamal Ortiz: I attached a link to the incident timeline and logs in our internal runbook (link omitted here). I can provide a CSV of error counts per minute for AcmeCorp.

Priya Nair: I'll coordinate with Finance now and update this thread with confirmation of the credit posting window.

Ariana Chen: thanks all — if no objections I'll send the customer note at 10:00 UTC and publish the status page update immediately after. If Legal or eng want to tweak anything else, please flag within the hour. :thumbsup:
